text.title: Breaking Change Deprecation Policy Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether anything outside the owning repository installs a published version, what kind of change is on the table, and how the slowest consumer picks up releases — to a full policy, a classification or codemod requirement, a window recomputation, or a skip.

decision-tree.root-question: Who consumes this component or token from a published, versioned release outside the repository that owns it?

branch.when: nothing outside this repository imports it — the rename lands in a single pull request

conclusion.verdict: skip: an atomic rename inside one repo needs no window; update the call sites in the same change

branch.when: the system is pre-1.0 with a published API-unstable contract, or nothing is versioned or tagged at all

conclusion.verdict: skip: there is no published version for consumers to remain on — route to design-system-governance to establish versioning and release tagging first

branch.when: external consumers install a published version and the change has not shipped yet
branch.question: What is actually changing in the release?

branch.when: a token value moves and a documented foreground/background pairing crosses below 4.5:1 body, 3:1 large text, or 3:1 for a UI boundary

conclusion.verdict: classify MAJOR however similar it looks, and record the before and after ratio for every affected pairing — contrast is not linear in perceptual similarity

branch.when: a symbol, prop or token key is renamed, or a prop default changes — the migration is mechanical

conclusion.verdict: ship a runnable codemod in the same release as the deprecation notice; without one, extend `removal_date` by a full additional consumer release cycle

branch.when: the change has not been checked against the enumerated MAJOR list at all

conclusion.verdict: classify before publishing: anything below MAJOR lands in every caret-ranged consumer's next install without a human reading the diff

branch.when: the change is classified against the enumerated list, no documented pairing regresses, and `consumer_teams` is known

conclusion.verdict: apply the full policy: classification, window sized on the slowest consumer, codemod, dev-only single warning, migration guide, and a usage-scan gate on removal

branch.when: the deprecation is already announced and the open question is the timeline or the removal
branch.question: How do the slowest consumers actually pick up a new version?

branch.when: at least one consumer ships a native binary whose adoption tail is measured in installed versions, not deploys

conclusion.verdict: size `deprecation_window_days` at two release cycles of that consumer measured on forced-update or version-adoption data — not store submission dates — and name which consumer set the floor

branch.when: consumers redeploy continuously, but the deprecated path warns on every render or the warning is present in production bundles

conclusion.verdict: keep the deprecated API functional for the whole window and emit exactly one dev-only warning per symbol per session, naming the replacement, `removal_date` and `migration_guide_ref`

branch.when: the window has elapsed and consumer teams report they are migrated

conclusion.verdict: do not remove on self-report: run a static scan across the consumer repository list and attach the command, the date and the repo list showing zero remaining imports or token references
